history.content: idk. got the promotion i wanted. felt nothing
Got it, the promotion landed and it felt like nothing. I can stay with that plain blankness, or we can see what it’s like for you.
everyone kept saying congrats. i just nodded. like watching it happen to someone else
That sounds more like being detached or far away than calm. Did it feel like you were just going through the motions, or more like you were outside the moment?
outside it i guess. i worked yrs for this. supposed to mean im finally somebody. and theres just. nothing there

That “nothing there” lands as a flat kind of distance, especially against how much this was supposed to mean. It sounds like the promotion was carrying a lot of identity with it, and then it didn’t light up the way it was meant to.
ya. and now im scared its always gonna be like this. chase a thing get it feel hollow. whats even the point of me

I want to check what you mean, gently. When you say that, is it more like being completely worn down and fed up, or are you having thoughts of harming yourself or not feeling safe? Either answer is okay to say here.
no nothing like that. im safe. just empty. tired of feeling empty
Thanks, that helps. This sounds like the empty tiredness is what’s in front right now, with the “what’s even the point” hanging behind it.
yeah thats it exactly. i thought the title would fix the empty. it didnt. nothing does
That sounds like disappointment meeting a very old emptiness, and the title had been holding a promise it couldn’t keep. I can stay with that, or we can leave it here for now.
an old emptiness ya. been there long b4 the job. job was just the latest thing i pinned it on
That helps, yes. The job sounds like the latest place you hoped the emptiness might change, while the emptiness itself has been around longer.
dunno what to do with that. but. saying it out loud helped a bit. didnt expect that
That makes sense. It sounds like naming it gave the emptiness a bit of room, even if it didn’t change it.
ya. thanks. gonna go sit with it. take care
Take care, and I’m glad this gave you a little room.
